heading: 8.4 Dimensioned × dimensioned — strip and assert
text:
### 8.4 Dimensioned × dimensioned — strip and assert [LUNI.8.4]

No unit algebra. `*` of two dimensioned values, `/` and `//` of two values of
different dimensions, `/` and `//` of a bare number by a dimensioned value, and `**` or `math.pow` with a dimensioned operand on either side
produce a result with no dimension DS can state. The compiler **must** refuse each
with `DS_VALIDATE_DIM_AMBIGUOUS`, under a `let` annotation too: an annotation
checks a type the value already has ([LUNI.8.6]). An author who wants the raw
numeric result strips the units on the operands first, and may assert a unit on
the result: `(r.w::Float * r.h::Float)::meter_squared`.

The strip yields base-unit numbers, and an assertion takes its number as being in
the unit it names ([LUNI.8.5]), so the scale of the result is the author's to state. A value of the
`time` dimension strips to nanoseconds ([LUNI.7.2]).

This rule applies to both scalar and complex dimensioned values. The built-in
library pre-declares common multiplication results (e.g. `watt` = `volt × ampere`,
`joule` = `newton × meter`), so those results have a unit to assert.

alloy.name: luni_8_4__annotation_admits_nothing
alloy.note: Two binops alike in their operands' dimensions and their operator are accepted or refused alike, whatever either is annotated with: 'under a `let` annotation too'. Derived: acceptance is a function of the dimensions and the operator alone, within the scope, and a rule that read the annotation fails it. What the annotation checks is [LUNI.8.6]'s, outside the model.

alloy.name: luni_8_4__no_unit_algebra
alloy.note: No accepted binop is a form with no statable dimension. A restatement of the accept rule's third exclusion, within the scope: it fails if the rule drops it or admits an annotated one.

alloy.name: luni_8_4__unstatable
alloy.note: The clause's list: `*` of two dimensioned values, `/` and `//` of two values of different dimensions and of a bare number by a dimensioned value, `**` with a dimensioned operand on either side; `math.pow` is `**` here. A transcription. The strip and the assertion on the result are [LUNI.8.5]'s and [LUNI.8.7.2]'s, outside the model; the code a refusal carries is not modelled.
